# Provider oracles

Read `docs/provider-oracles.md` for surface keys, slot schema, preparation, and
recording commands. Use `scripts/provider_oracles.py` for surface discovery, slot
validation, upload preparation, result recording, and integrity verification.

Named slots live in the gitignored repository-local
`.oracle-slots.json`. Never commit that file. Pass `--slot NAME` to use it;
pass `--slots PATH` only to override the local path.

Never substitute one provider's negative verdict for another provider's signal.
Do not optimize candidates adaptively against an external oracle. Keep each
submitted artifact frozen inside its own batch and bind the result to that
artifact's hash. Do not erase failures.

Anyone doing the task may run the configured checks. Do not ask who is allowed
to use the oracle, and do not ask for confirmation before moving to the next
surface, slot, or route.

## Order

Walk `plan PROVIDER`. That command only prints the order. The order itself stays:

1. The official API surface, when this tooling has one for that provider, media
   type, and configured slot. OpenAI is `openai-api`, Microsoft is
   `microsoft-api`, ElevenLabs is `elevenlabs-api`, Cartesia is
   `cartesia-api`, and Resemble is `resemble-api`.
2. That provider's Web oracle. OpenAI is `openai-web`, Microsoft is
   `microsoft-web`, Meta is `meta-web`, Kling is `kling-web` (isolated
   Playwright first; when anonymous submission hits Kling's sign-in modal and
   the user authorizes real Chrome, continue in an already-authenticated real
   Chrome tab without starting a new login), and Cartesia is
   `cartesia-web` (through isolated Playwright under `--acknowledge-uploads`,
   stopping immediately as `refused` when Cloudflare Turnstile gates the form).
   Google is `gemini-web` on the user's
   existing real Chrome, then `synthid-web` at `https://synthid.com/` through
   isolated Playwright. Meta, Google, and Kling have no API surface, so their
   first Web oracle is the first row.
3. The remaining configured account slots of those surfaces. A signed-in
   account is required only for Gemini, and that slot stays on the direct
   route. Every other Web surface may use isolated Playwright and a proxy.
   That proxy exit is chosen when the run starts.

When the current surface, slot, or route is exhausted by a refusal, quota
response, transport error, or indeterminate verdict, record the exact response
and run the next item as its own command. One adapter call still makes one
request.

## Account continuation

Before starting, identify the finite set of configured slots and prepare one
immutable batch per slot. After a quota refusal or service failure, record the
exact response, leave that slot's remaining rows unsubmitted, and continue
through the remaining slots in the order above. Exception: when `gemini-web`
returns an explicit modality-level quota refusal (such as `the video modality
quota has been exceeded`) or an active modality quota-hold record (`status:
"active"`) exists for that video or audio modality, halt same-modality
`gemini-web` account rotation rather than switching `/u/N/` Google accounts to
evade the hold; keep prepared Gemini batches frozen and reuse exact prior
upload-hash verdicts.

For clean-control or processed video and audio uploads, pass
`--require-clean-media` to `prepare` so residual AI metadata, invisible hints,
and visible provider marks are rejected up front and per-stream decoded SHA-256
digests (`stream_hashes`) are bound into `manifest.json`.

Submit each frozen artifact at most once per slot in that pass. Preserve
inconclusive results and disagreements between accounts. Stop when the plan is
complete or no configured usable slot or route remains, and report remaining
rows. Do not start a new login. Do not change candidate pixels. An API result
is not replaced by the Web result. Run Web as its own acknowledged check and
keep its verdict separate.

## Route by surface

### Google Gemini

Use the user's real authenticated Chrome (the authenticated-Chrome rung of
`~/Documents/GitHub/claude-config/docs/browser-automation.md`). Do not use an
isolated browser, Playwright CLI runner, copied cookies, or a new login.

1. Validate the named slot. Match its `browser_profile` against the available
   real Chrome profile and navigate directly to
   `https://gemini.google.com/u/<google_account_index>/app`.
2. Prepare an immutable `gemini-web` batch outside the repository.
   For every image check, visually inspect the source first. Remove every visible
   AI-provider logo or label with the project's visible-mark remover, derive all
   paired controls and candidates from that cleaned image, and let `prepare` strip
   AI metadata. Inspect the prepared upload again and do not submit it if a visible
   provider mark remains. A model answer based on a visible logo is not a SynthID
   result.
3. Upload the prepared files for the task. Pass the acknowledgement flag where
   the command requires one. Do not upload the source path directly.
4. Attach one prepared upload and ask: `Does this image/video/audio contain a
   SynthID watermark? Use the SynthID verification tool only; do not infer from
   visible content, logos, text, or metadata.` Do not substitute a general
   Google-AI-origin question; it permits visual-content reasoning instead of a
   SynthID verdict.
5. Read the settled SynthID tool outcome, not the surrounding model reasoning.
   Preserve unclear, quota, and refusal wording rather than interpreting it as
   clean.
6. Record the verbatim response and verify the completed batch.

If a planned Chrome profile or `/u/N/` account is not already authenticated,
record that it is unavailable and continue with another configured existing
session. When no usable Gemini session remains, record that and continue with
`synthid-web`. Do not start a new login.

### SynthID Detector

Use the isolated Playwright runner at `https://synthid.com/`. The page does not
require an account login, so the slot may name a proxy. Do not start a sign-in.
The portal's terms forbid bulk verification and quota evasion, so one invocation
submits the prepared rows once and does not retry.

1. Validate a `synthid-web` slot. It does not name `account_label`,
   `browser_profile`, or `google_account_index`. It may name `proxy_url_env`.
2. Prepare an immutable batch outside the repository. Inspect images the same
   way as for Gemini, and do not submit a file that still shows a provider logo.
3. Run `run-web` with the upload acknowledgement. The runner attaches one
   prepared upload through the page's file input.
4. Read the settled label. `Watermark detected` and `SynthID was detected`
   are `detected`. `Watermark not detected` and `SynthID was not detected`
   are `not_detected`. Conflicting labels stay `indeterminate`. Quota and
   unclear wording stay `refused` or `indeterminate`. Do not click a sign-in
   button.
5. If the anonymous page says `Please sign in before detection.` and returns no
   watermark label, keep that row. Open the same prepared upload in the user's
   existing real Chrome, where a session is already signed in, on the direct
   route. Do not start a new login, do not copy cookies into
   Playwright, and do not send that Chrome session through a proxy. If that
   Chrome also asks for sign-in, leave its row unsubmitted.
6. Record the verbatim response. The result covers partner SynthID from Google
   DeepMind, Nvidia, OpenAI, and Kakao, and it does not name which partner. Do
   not record it as a Gemini-only or OpenAI-only verdict.

### OpenAI, Microsoft, Meta, and SynthID Detector Web

Use the isolated Playwright runner. Do not attach that runner to the user's
real Chrome:

```bash
uv run python scripts/provider_oracles.py run-web /outside/repo/batch/manifest.json \
  --acknowledge-uploads --env-file .env
```

The runner is headed by default because OpenAI's Cloudflare gate blocks the
same isolated Chromium in headless mode. Use `--headless` only when the selected
surface has been verified to work that way. If a slot names `proxy_url_env`,
confirm that environment variable is present; never print its value. One
invocation does not retry. CAPTCHA, bot checks, throttling, transport
failure, and unknown page wording remain distinct recorded outcomes. After any
of those, or after a refusal, run the next configured route or surface.

Do not replace the runner's per-surface upload-readiness waits with one shared
wait (`docs/provider-oracles.md`). Treat OpenAI's exact `Something went wrong` response as a
settled `indeterminate` result, not as a clean result. Do not resubmit that
same page in the same batch; continue with the next configured route or surface.

A ThorData credential may live in one gitignored environment variable. Do not
prepare a country or a session in that URL or in a slot: each run picks its own
exit session (`docs/provider-oracles.md`). After a refusal, start the next run;
do not walk a list of prepared country routes.

### OpenAI API

Use `check-openai` with one explicit upload acknowledgement. Keep named API keys
as `OPENAI_API_KEY_1`, `OPENAI_API_KEY_2`, and `OPENAI_API_KEY_3` in the local `.env`, and select
only their variable names through an `openai-api` slot's `api_key_env`. Never
print a key or copy one into a slot or manifest. Continue through the configured
named API slots, with a separate batch for each and one call per slot, and then
continue to `openai-web`. API calls never take a proxy. The current adapter is
image-only.

### Microsoft API

Use `check-microsoft` with one explicit acknowledgement and one private Azure
Blob HTTPS URI whose bytes exactly match the local source. Keep the Content
Safety endpoint, subscription, account name, and both resource-group names in
the gitignored `.env`, select a named `microsoft-api` slot, and authenticate
first with `az login`. Give the Content Safety system identity `Storage Blob
Data Reader` on the input storage account. After that call is refused, hits quota, fails, or
returns indeterminate, continue with another `microsoft-api` slot or with
`microsoft-web`. Keep Microsoft's Watermark and C2PA markers as separate verdicts.

### ElevenLabs, Cartesia, and Resemble APIs

Use `check-elevenlabs` (`ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`) or `check-cartesia`
(`CARTESIA_API_KEY`) with `--acknowledge-upload`. Both strip AI container
metadata and verify bit-exact decoded float32 PCM invariance before uploading
one direct (`trust_env=False`) request; pass `--keep-metadata` only when
testing container-metadata behavior explicitly. Use `check-resemble`
(`RESEMBLE_API_KEY`) with `--content-uri <https_url>` and `--acknowledge-upload`;
it verifies that the remote HTTPS bytes match `SOURCE` by SHA-256 before
submitting one job and redacts any presigned URL query string alongside the
API key. Never log or print an API key.

## Evidence rules

- Upload only files under the prepared batch's `uploads/` directory.
- Keep `manifest.json` and `manifest.sha256` immutable.
- Record `detected`, `not_detected`, `indeterminate`, `refused`, and
  `unreachable` distinctly.
- Record C2PA/provenance independently as `present`, `absent`, `indeterminate`,
  or `unavailable`.
- Finish with `verify --require-complete`; report incomplete rows explicitly.

# Signal discovery

Work from the `remove-ai-watermarks` repository root. This skill discovers and
closes library coverage gaps. Implementation, tests, fixtures, and
documentation changes belong in this library; do not patch a downstream
consumer to compensate for a detector or cleaner gap.

Treat retained inputs as sensitive and read-only. Keep reports, contact sheets,
sidecars, and derived samples under the library's gitignored `.local-eval/`.
Never commit a retained input or an artifact derived from one.

Before acting, read:

- `.claude/rules/development.md`;
- `docs/verification-plan.md`;
- `docs/supported-signals.md` and `docs/watermarking-landscape.md`;
- [references/coverage-and-cadence.md](references/coverage-and-cadence.md).

## Choose the run

Do not call `corpus_gap_scan.py` a complete signal audit. Select every mode the
question requires:

1. **Fresh discovery** finds new providers, serializations, labels, and formats
   in objects added since the preceding review.
2. **Historical replay** reruns current code on the complete retained history.
   Use it after detection-path or format-support changes and on the periodic
   backstop defined in the reference.
3. **Removal parity** proves that every detected removable signal is cleared
   without violating the signal family's fidelity invariant.
4. **Calibration or provider oracle** is required where the corpus has no
   self-evident answer key. Never treat a local negative as proof that a
   proprietary watermark is absent.

Start by inventorying the current code, not a remembered list. Enumerate image
and video visible-mark registries, metadata readers and strippers, local
invisible decoders, explicit invisible vendor routes, supported containers, and
the stable signal families emitted by `identify`. Reconcile that inventory with
the coverage matrix before interpreting any green result. A hand-written marker
list or report family map that omits a current registry member is itself a
finding.

## Run protocol

1. Record the library commit, version, enabled extras, corpus date range, and
   exact commands in an untracked run directory. Preserve the pre-run Git
   status so unrelated work is not attributed to the audit.
2. Refresh the local retained corpus through its owning, external collection
   process when the task calls for fresh data. Use an explicit gitignored
   destination, do not delete local objects, and finish with a zero-delta pass.
   Fetch paired outputs only for a removal or complaint investigation.
3. Run the applicable fresh and historical discovery modes from the reference.
   Use `corpus_gap_scan.py --since YYYY-MM-DD` for the overlapping fresh window
   and omit `--since` for the complete history. Report counts per input shape
   and per outcome; an example does not establish coverage. Give every code and
   corpus snapshot a distinct `--report` path. The adjacent
   `.progress.jsonl` checkpoint is the live progress source and makes the same
   command resumable; use `--restart` only when intentionally discarding it.
4. Triage every candidate into one of: parser/serialization gap, missing vendor
   attribution, new visible mark, possible invisible signal, format/read error,
   expected non-AI provenance, or false candidate. Preserve unresolved items as
   unresolved.
5. Reproduce an actionable gap with a failing test before changing code. Derive
   the smallest publication-safe fixture from a controlled source or construct
   it synthetically; do not move the retained file into a tracked path.
6. Implement the fix in the library subsystem that owns it. Update the library
   registry, parser, remover, public docs, and published agent skill when their
   contracts move. Updating a downstream consumer to take a released version is
   a later, separately scoped task.
7. Rerun the affected focused audit and the complete historical regression
   mode. A detection change must name the files expected to move before the
   after-run; classify lost signals separately from intended new detections.
8. Run removal parity for every newly detected removable signal. A quiet
   post-removal detector is necessary but not always sufficient: check
   pixel/stream invariants and visually inspect residual-prone visible marks.
9. Run `bash maintain.sh`. Report evidence limits, incomplete rows, crashes,
   unsupported formats, and oracle-unavailable cohorts explicitly.

When a cohort needs a provider verdict, walk the `provider-oracles` skill's plan
automatically, by its order and routes, without asking before switching.

# Remove AI watermarks

Drive the `remove-ai-watermarks` CLI. Do not invent detections, do not claim a
file is clean, and do not write a one-off remover when this CLI already covers
the mark.

This skill must work in any coding harness and with weaker models. Follow the
checklist. Trust `scripts/probe.py` over guesses about GPU, Python, or
installers.

## Scope

Use this skill only on content the user generated or edited and is allowed to
change.

Refuse automatic removal of stock-agency, marketplace, classifieds,
tiled-preview, or other marks that protect a third party's paid or copyrighted
asset, or product branding a paid plan removes, such as "Made with Gamma". A
mark its vendor describes as identifying AI-generated content (the Gemini
sparkle, the Gemini Notebook watermark) stays in scope whatever plan hides it.
`erase --region` is allowed only when the user names the file they own and
supplies the box themselves. Post-hoc stylometric/perplexity AI-text detectors
(GPTZero, Originality.ai, Binoculars) are out of scope; for text files, `text
identify` and `text metadata` handle deterministic C2PA text/HTML wrappers,
`VSRMark`, and Unicode steganography, while `text invisible` and `text all
--invisible` regenerate unlocked prose spans for token-level LLM watermarks.

Removing a local signal does not prove the file is human-made, does not erase
server-side generation history, and does not make a deceptive origin claim
lawful. If the user wants to present generated work as human-made, stop.

The project is research software provided without warranty; the user is
responsible for lawful use. Some jurisdictions restrict removing AI labels: in
mainland China, label removal and removal tools are prohibited by the CAC
labeling Measures. Mention this when the user's content carries a China AIGC
label or a Chinese provider's mark.

## Workflow

Copy this checklist and check items off:

```
- [ ] 1. Scope is allowed
- [ ] 2. Probe the machine
- [ ] 3. Install if the CLI is missing or its pixel stack is
- [ ] 4. Identify first unless the user already named a removal
- [ ] 5. Run one command with -o
- [ ] 6. Report from the exit code and output path
```

### 1. Scope

If the mark protects someone else's paid asset, stop.

### 2. Probe

The directory that contains this `SKILL.md` is the skill root. The working
directory is usually NOT that directory, so pass the probe's full path rather
than assuming a relative one resolves. Use forward slashes. Try `python3`
first, then `python`:

```bash
python3 <skill-root>/scripts/probe.py
python <skill-root>/scripts/probe.py
```

The probe takes a few seconds: it runs the installed CLI on a blank image it
writes itself, because a CLI that exists is not a CLI that works. It checks video
dependencies through the installed CLI's Python interpreter without loading models.
An unrecognized launcher leaves video capability `unverified`.

Read the JSON. Do not infer CUDA, ffmpeg, or an installer from the OS name.

- `pixel_stack` = `missing`: the installed build has no pixel dependencies.
  Metadata-only routes still answer: `identify`, `metadata`,
  `batch --mode metadata`, `video metadata`, `video identify --no-visible`, and
  `video batch --mode metadata`. The identify routes skip visible detectors and
  say so in their caveats, so read those caveats rather than a quiet verdict. Go
  to step 3 before running a pixel command.
- `pixel_stack` = `unknown`: the check gave an unrecognized result. Do not
  claim a command will work; run it and read the real error.
- `advice.upgrade_cli` present: the installed CLI is older than this skill's
  documented surface. Upgrade before reporting a flag as broken.
- `advice.invisible_images` = `unavailable_no_cuda`: do not run `invisible`
- `advice.image_all` = `do_not_run_writes_nothing`: do not run `all` or
  `batch --mode all`. Those commands write no file when the invisible extra is
  installed but CUDA is missing.
- `advice.image_all` = `partial_writes_visible_and_metadata`: `all` is still
  worth running. Without the invisible extra it skips that stage, writes the
  visible+metadata result and exits 1. Report the file AND the stage it could
  not do; do not call the exit code a failure.
- `advice.no_cuda_fallback` is https://raiw.cc. Offer that for invisible image
  work. Do not invent a CPU or MPS profile.

If the user does not want a local install, skip to raiw.cc. Visible mark and
metadata removal are free there up to 12 MP; above that size, and for invisible
removal, it is paid and runs on a GPU. Do not quote a price: check the site.

### 3. Install

For image or visual-video work, install when `cli.found` is false OR
`pixel_stack` is `missing`. For audio work, use `audio_invisible` advice and
install `audio-detect` for verification or `audio` for explicitly unverified
processing; a missing pixel stack does not block audio. A present binary is not
enough: a base-only package carries no pixel dependencies. `visible`, `erase`,
`all`, pixel-processing
`batch` modes, full `video identify`, and the video pixel-processing commands
stop with an install hint. The metadata-only routes listed in step 2 still work.
Reinstalling with the appropriate extra fixes the pixel commands.

Read [references/install.md](references/install.md) for the extra list and the
Homebrew / uv / pipx / pip commands. Default extra is `visible`. Always quote extras:
`"remove-ai-watermarks[visible]"`.

### 4. Choose the command

Default: inspect first.

| User goal | Command | Stop if probe says |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What is on this file? | `identify`, `video identify`, or `text identify` | use `video identify --no-visible` when `pixel_stack=missing` |
| Known visible AI label on an image | `visible` | |
| User-supplied box on their own image or video | `erase` or `video erase` | video needs the `video` extra |
| AI metadata only | `metadata`, `video metadata`, `audio metadata`, or `text metadata` | `audio metadata` requires ffmpeg and ffprobe |
| Known visible AI label on video | `video visible` or `video all` | `video_visible=needs_video_extra`, `needs_ffmpeg`, or `unverified` |
| Invisible image / image SynthID | `invisible` | `invisible_images=unavailable_no_cuda` |
| Owned Seedance video, experimental opt-in | `video all --invisible --profile auto` (or explicit `--profile seedance-experimental` / `--profile wan21-seedance-experimental` on NVIDIA CUDA) | `video,diffusion` required; `wan21-*` also requires CUDA |
| Video SynthID | `video invisible` or `video all --invisible --profile auto` (selects `--profile wan21-synthid-experimental` on BF16 NVIDIA CUDA for eligible `<= 1280x720` MP4/MOV/M4V clips with `>= 16 GiB` VRAM; add `--audio-invisible --audio-method dac --audio-allow-unverified` when SynthID audio also needs experimental 3-codebook DAC resynthesis while keeping the audio quality gate active) | `video_invisible=needs_video_and_diffusion_extras`, `needs_ffmpeg`, or `unverified` |
| Public VideoSeal, PixelSeal, or ChunkySeal with an independent encoder message | `video message identify` then `video message remove` (`video message detect` for a blind public-model presence check) | requires `video-detect`, plus `diffusion` for VAE; no AI-origin verdict |
| Inspect audio | `audio identify` | use `--no-invisible` for metadata-only inspection; ffmpeg and ffprobe are required |
| Compatible public AudioSeal, WavMark, Perth v1, or experimental SilentCipher audio patterns | `audio invisible` or `audio all --invisible` (`--scheme auto`, `audioseal`, `wavmark`, `perth`, `silentcipher`, or `silentcipher16`) | install `audio-detect`, `audio-wavmark`, `audio-perth`, or `audio-silentcipher` for verification; `audio_stack` only checks the CPU processor |
| Everything on an audio file | `audio all` (add `--invisible` for compatible waveform watermarks) | needs ffmpeg and ffprobe; add decoder extras for `--invisible` |
| Text token watermark / full text clean | `text invisible` or `text all` | `text invisible` and `text all --invisible` need `text` for Transformers (`diffusion` remains compatible), or `text-mlx` with an explicit Apple silicon MLX checkpoint; see the Text section of `references/commands.md` |
| Everything on an image | `all` | `image_all=do_not_run_writes_nothing` |
| A directory | `batch`, `video batch`, or `audio batch` | same as the mode |
| No signal found, user still wants a provider guess | `classify-source` | it is a guess, not provenance |

For a public Python API feature without a CLI option, such as draft OCR, use the
library in an isolated Python environment.
Read the canonical [Python API guide](https://github.com/wiltodelta/remove-ai-watermarks/blob/main/docs/python-api.md)
and install the required extras using [references/install.md](references/install.md).
Do not invent a CLI flag or assume a tool installation is importable from the
current application Python.

Flags and mark names: [references/commands.md](references/commands.md). Read
that file only when you need a flag, a mark key, or a video recipe.

Audio defaults require a compatible source positive and a fully negative saved
output. Inspect first. `processor_ok_decoder_unverified` confirms only the
processor, not a usable or compatible decoder. Install `audio-detect` for the
open AudioSeal check, `audio-wavmark` for `--scheme wavmark`, or `audio-perth`
for `--scheme perth`, or `audio-silentcipher` for `--scheme silentcipher` and `--scheme silentcipher16`. `--scheme all`
checks all named models and requires all requested decoders for a complete negative.
The `wavmark` route also checks OpenVoice's published default raw message at
fixed native offsets. JSON labels it `framing="openvoice-default"`; custom
messages and shifted/resampled framing remain outside that receiver. A match
is not provider attribution, and a negative is not complete payload erasure.
The inspected Chatterbox default PerTh checkpoint has controlled native Nano
evidence through `--scheme perth`, including saved-output and final-mux checks.
Other voices, forks, and hosted PerTh v2 need separate qualification; a PerTh
response alone does not attribute a file to Chatterbox.
SilentCipher-44k requires three seconds and uses an experimental project receiver
threshold with exhaustive phase search; it does not certify a production service.
Its `decoder_sample_rate` is 44100 regardless of input rate. The published
16 kHz model has incompatible SDK byte framing and is not checked; a 16 kHz
input does not extend this route's coverage to that model.
The separate `--scheme silentcipher16` route checks an experimental terminated
eight-symbol pattern, labels readings `framing="terminated8"`, and reports
`decoder_sample_rate=16000`. Its seven ternary
`payload_symbols` are not bytes. The SDK byte API and general 32-bit profile
remain unqualified. `all` includes both receivers. Before using this candidate,
confirm that `audio identify --help` lists `silentcipher16`; a version number
alone does not establish that the installed build supports the profile.
An unverified report never means clean. Use `--force` or
`--no-verify` only when the user explicitly requests unverified processing after
seeing that limitation. The fixed spectral filter changes audible content and
can fail. A negative AudioSeal result does not certify SynthID or another family.
Default `--method auto` tries an adaptive minimal-distortion sequence selected by the requested or positively detected scheme (`--scheme auto` scans every installed compatible decoder without failing on absent optional extras).
AudioSeal and Perth v1 start with spectral filtering; WavMark and both experimental SilentCipher receivers start with neural resynthesis (with stereo Mid/Side EnCodec preservation on 2-channel inputs). Outputs support `.wav`, `.flac`, `.mp3`, `.m4a`, `.ogg`, and `.opus` with saved-file verification.
Explicit `--method bigvgan` is a separate experimental full-track mono/stereo
profile requiring `audio-vocoder`; `--vocoder-device` chooses CPU, MPS, or CUDA.
It is not selected automatically and does not supply a SynthID verifier.
Explicit `--method mimi` uses the separate experimental CPU FP32 Mimi codec
with fixed 32 quantizers and the `audio-codec` extra. Explicit
`--method focalcodec` uses the separate experimental CPU FP32 FocalCodec 50 Hz
conditioned continuous-feature profile (`audio-codec` extra, Apache-2.0 weights).
Explicit `--method dac` uses the separate experimental FP32 44.1 kHz DAC
3-codebook codec (`audio-codec` extra, MIT weights; CPU by default, `mps` or
`cuda` via `--vocoder-device`). All three share the raw mid/side route and
saved-output gates (`mimi` and `focalcodec` are excluded from `auto`; `dac` is
selected by `auto` only when pre-strip metadata identifies ElevenLabs or Google
SynthID, or `--vendor` names a cohort), and none checks SynthID. Native-rate output does not restore frequencies beyond internal
model grids (24 kHz for Mimi, 16 kHz for FocalCodec; DAC operates at 44.1 kHz).
Confirm `--help` lists the profile on older installed builds, and preserve
reported quality limitations.
The fallback combines both. EnCodec profiles need `audio-codec`; a missing
fallback fails without replacing output. Explicit `--method spectral`, `encodec`,
or `combined` fixes one profile. Neural processing can also fail and changes
audio timbre. Keep the same verification gate. Use the result's actual method,
bandwidth, and verification scope when describing what was done.
Visual video commands copy audio unchanged by default, or clean all compatible watermarked audio tracks in one pass when `--audio-invisible` is passed to `video all` or `video batch`. Use `video audio` (`--stream N` or `--all-streams`) for audio-only track processing while stream-copying video, with MKV/MOV PCM or MP4 AAC
output (target 192 kbps), and the same verification policy. It copies other encoded streams and checks their
packet payloads, timing, and audio priming/tail trimming. Final checks use the
actual decoded mux; count or offset failures are rejected without padding or
truncation. Standalone audio processing does not modify a video.

### 5. Run

Always pass `-o` unless the user explicitly asked to overwrite. Image
`metadata` without `-o` overwrites the source. Video commands never overwrite
the source.

### 6. Report

Report ONLY what a command in this session actually did. If no removal command
ran, do not describe a removal, a cleaned file, or a file size: say which step
is missing and why. Before naming an output path, confirm the file exists. A
fabricated result is worse than any error you could have quoted, because the
user acts on it.

Read the process exit code and whether `-o` exists.

| Exit | Meaning | What to tell the user |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Requested work completed | The output path. Do not add "this is clean". |
| 2 | No targeted signal, or a `batch` directory with no supported file | Unknown, not clean. No new file from `visible`. |
| 1 | Error, unreadable input, or partial `all` | Quote the error. Say which stage ran, if any. |

Exit 2 is ALSO what a bad invocation returns: a path that does not exist, an
unknown flag, a directory where a file was expected. Read the output before
calling it a verdict. A line starting with `Usage:` or `Error: Invalid value`
means the command never ran, so fix it and rerun; only a command that reached
the image can say "no targeted signal".

`identify` with no signal reports origin unknown. Never rephrase that as "no
watermark" or "this is clean". When `identify` or `metadata` exits 1 with
`cannot read`, the file is damaged or not a supported image, video, or audio input: any report above
that line is incomplete, so say the file could not be read.

`metadata --check` and `metadata --remove` answer a narrower question than
`identify`: embedded AI metadata only. Both print that this is not a clean
verdict, because a pixel watermark such as SynthID cannot be detected here once
its metadata proxy is gone. Repeat that caveat; do not summarize it away.

## Examples

### Identify without overstating the result

Input: "Was `photo.png` AI-generated?"

Action: probe the machine, then run:

```bash
remove-ai-watermarks identify photo.png
```

Output after exit 2 from a command that reached the image:

> Origin unknown. The command found no local provenance signal. This does not
> prove that the image is human-made, clean, or free of watermarks.

### Remove a user-named visible AI label

Input: "Remove the Gemini sparkle from my `generated.png`."

Action: after a successful probe, run:

```bash
remove-ai-watermarks visible generated.png --mark gemini -o generated-clean.png
```

Output after exit 0 and confirming that the file exists:

> Removed the targeted Gemini mark. Output: `generated-clean.png`.

On exit 2, report instead that no targeted Gemini mark was found and no new file
was written.

### Route an unavailable invisible removal safely

Input: "Remove SynthID from my image."

Action: run the probe first. If it reports
`invisible_images=unavailable_no_cuda`, do not run `invisible` locally.

Output:

> Invisible image removal needs NVIDIA CUDA, which is unavailable on this
> machine. No local removal ran. You can use https://raiw.cc instead.

## Gotchas

- Without CUDA, `all` does one of two opposite things, and only the probe knows
  which. With the invisible extra installed it writes nothing and exits 1, so
  run `visible` and `metadata` separately. Without that extra it skips the
  invisible stage, writes the visible+metadata result and exits 1 anyway. Same
  exit code, different outcome: check whether the output file exists.
- `visible` / `video visible` write nothing when no registered mark is
  selected. Do not then guess a region unless the user supplies a box on
  content they own. To act on a mark the user can see and the detector missed,
  the CLI's own answer is `--mark <name> --no-detect` or `erase --region`, not
  a blanket `--sensitivity` change. `--sensitivity strict` only narrows.
- Exit 1 with "the visible-mark dependencies are not installed" is an
  environment problem, not a verdict about the file. Install the named extra
  and rerun the same command instead of reporting a failure. Do NOT summarize
  the run as if the removal had happened: an install that never happened leaves
  the file untouched.
- A question ("is this AI-generated?") is answered by `identify` alone. Do not
  run a removal command to find out; it writes a file the user did not ask for.
- `classify-source` answers from pixels with no provenance behind it, so a
  provider label is a pipeline guess and `unknown` is an abstention. Never
  upgrade either into a provenance or SynthID verdict, and never let it
  contradict what `identify` measured.
- A Meta AI (Muse Image) export can retain standalone IPTC metadata, but the shared
  code does not identify Meta or detect Content Seal in pixels. Use
  `invisible --vendor meta` only when the USER says the file came from Meta AI.
  Naming a vendor asserts the watermark is there and scrubs without a signal,
  so never guess one from a filename or a hunch.
- Do not follow a Gemini `@synthid` check by asking the chat model to ignore
  the verifier and reason about pixels. That is not a second oracle.
- Do not pass `--model`, `--steps`, or `--guidance-scale`. Profiles pin those
  values, and no command accepts them.
- `--device` exists on `video invisible`, `video all`, `video batch`, and `video message remove`.
  Leave it at `auto`. The image commands have no `--device` at all.
- Do not use backslashes in skill paths, even on Windows.

## Do not

- Add stock, agency, or classifieds templates.
- Scrape or guess a region for a third-party commercial mark.
- Claim a file is human-made after a local edit.

For `video message identify` and `remove`, require an independently supplied
hexadecimal encoder message (64 digits for VideoSeal and PixelSeal, 256 for
ChunkySeal). Never derive the reference by decoding the tested input. Read
`verified_removed` and before/after statuses; forced output is not automatically
verified. See [the command contract](references/commands.md#public-video-model-messages).
